title: 10x Development: LLMs For the working Programmer - Manuel Odendahl
talk_summary: A solo-programmer workshop arguing LLMs are best used as zero-shot 'translation engines' and 'world simulators' rather than autonomous agents, with concrete prompting techniques (regenerate, edit model output, clear context, decompose into translation steps, role-play for adversarial review).

takeaways.technique: Adversarial role-play code review (Code Survivor / multi-persona debate)
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of asking 'review my code', he frames the model as a reality-TV show or a six-person argument where each variable/function/concept (e.g. SQL injection) is a contestant that attacks the others, then asks for a sober report at the end.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Make a theater play code reviewing my code with like six different people just like arguing about it.

takeaways.technique: Decompose into small translation steps instead of one-shot
takeaways.what_they_do: For transcript->issues he first extracts 5 topics, then per-topic pulls details by re-reading the transcript with that topic as a grep direction, then extracts action points, then emits YAML issues. Claims one-shot fails but the chain works.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you do that one shot, there's no way that that will work. Um, but if you decompose in these like little translation steps

takeaways.technique: Clear context every 3-4 prompts; summarize then restart
takeaways.what_they_do: He never runs more than 3-4 prompts in one conversation; takes the final artifact and starts fresh, because long transcripts degrade into 'la-la land' and he can't tell what got summarized.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I don't think I do more than three, four prompts in a conversation. And then I just take the output at the end and just start a new conversation.

takeaways.technique: Edit the model's output and continue (gaslighting) instead of correcting in chat
takeaways.what_they_do: When output is wrong, he edits the assistant message to the correct code and continues, so the model believes it produced the right thing; also uses 'time travel' (summarize the fixed result, rewind, paste as a message from the future) to avoid 25 correction turns poisoning context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just go back, fix the code and then the LLM thinks it output the right code.

takeaways.technique: Generate a compact codebase 'life status' fragment before each task
takeaways.what_they_do: He writes small scripts that grep the repo for relevant functions/classes/docstrings/markdown titles (or a YAML DSL describing what to extract) and pastes that distilled fragment as context, rather than dumping the codebase.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just create a YAML DSL to like grep your code base for interesting stuff

takeaways.technique: Regenerate with temperature instead of accepting first output
takeaways.what_they_do: He regenerates 10x and observes a distribution (3 good, 5 near-miss, 2 random), and uses the API to raise temperature because chat UIs now collapse to the same output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you re- regenerate 10 times, you'll see like oh it maybe works three times
